answer: Pin each identity to one physical location by latency triangulation: every epoch it must answer timed pings from several far-flung beacons, and the round-trip fingerprint, tight as a strung pearl, betrays where it truly sits. A farm packed in one datacenter emits the same violet-shifted timing signature across all its clones, so they collapse into a single identity. The cost is non-transferable: you cannot whisper your true location to a twin or bulk-buy genuinely distributed hardware, and a thousand fakes in one rack still ping as one place, so scale buys the attacker nothing.
